narration.en: Before 1991 the government ran airlines, hotels, bakeries and even watch factories. Should it? Privatisation asks that question.
narration.kn: 1991ಕ್ಕೆ ಮೊದಲು ಸರ್ಕಾರ ವಿಮಾನಯಾನ, ಹೋಟೆಲ್, ಬೇಕರಿ, ಗಡಿಯಾರ ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆಗಳನ್ನೂ ನಡೆಸುತ್ತಿತ್ತು. ಅದು ಸರಿಯೇ? ಖಾಸಗೀಕರಣ ಈ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ ಕೇಳುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Privatisation means shedding the ownership or management of a government-owned enterprise. It can be done by withdrawing the government from ownership and management, or by outright sale. Selling part of the equity of public sector enterprises to the public is called disinvestment. The aim was to improve financial discipline and modernisation and to attract private capital and managerial skill.
body.kn: ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ಉದ್ಯಮದ ಒಡೆತನ ಅಥವಾ ನಿರ್ವಹಣೆಯನ್ನು ಬಿಟ್ಟುಕೊಡುವುದೇ ಖಾಸಗೀಕರಣ. ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕ ಉದ್ಯಮಗಳ ಷೇರುಗಳ ಒಂದು ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಜನರಿಗೆ ಮಾರುವುದು ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಹಿಂತೆಗೆತ (ನಿರ್ಹೂಡಿಕೆ).

points.en: Disinvestment: sale of part of PSU equity to the public
Aim: efficiency, financial discipline, private capital and skills

narration.en: Privatisation means shedding the ownership or management of a government-owned enterprise. It can be done by withdrawing the government from ownership and management, or by outright sale. Selling part of the equity of public sector enterprises to the public is called disinvestment. The aim was to improve financial discipline and modernisation and to attract private capital and managerial skill.
narration.kn: ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ಉದ್ಯಮದ ಒಡೆತನ ಅಥವಾ ನಿರ್ವಹಣೆಯನ್ನು ಬಿಟ್ಟುಕೊಡುವುದೇ ಖಾಸಗೀಕರಣ. ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕ ಉದ್ಯಮಗಳ ಷೇರುಗಳ ಒಂದು ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಜನರಿಗೆ ಮಾರುವುದು ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಹಿಂತೆಗೆತ (ನಿರ್ಹೂಡಿಕೆ).

title.en: On the board: Disinvestment in numbers

say.en: The government owns all 10 crore shares of a public sector company.
It sells 2.5 crore shares, a quarter, to the public at 80 rupees each.
The government keeps majority ownership: this is disinvestment, not full privatisation.
Efficient profit-makers got autonomy as Maharatnas, Navratnas and Miniratnas.

body.en: To improve efficiency and help them compete globally, the government gave some profit-making public sector enterprises special status as Maharatnas, Navratnas and Miniratnas. These enterprises got greater managerial and operational autonomy in taking decisions, so they could run more efficiently while remaining in the public sector.
body.kn: ದಕ್ಷತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಲು ಕೆಲವು ಲಾಭದಾಯಕ ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕ ಉದ್ಯಮಗಳಿಗೆ ಮಹಾರತ್ನ, ನವರತ್ನ, ಮಿನಿರತ್ನ ಸ್ಥಾನ ನೀಡಲಾಯಿತು. ಇವುಗಳಿಗೆ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ ಕೈಗೊಳ್ಳುವಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಸ್ವಾಯತ್ತತೆ ದೊರೆಯಿತು.

points.en: Status gives greater operational and managerial autonomy

narration.en: To improve efficiency and help them compete globally, the government gave some profit-making public sector enterprises special status as Maharatnas, Navratnas and Miniratnas. These enterprises got greater managerial and operational autonomy in taking decisions, so they could run more efficiently while remaining in the public sector.
narration.kn: ದಕ್ಷತೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಲು ಕೆಲವು ಲಾಭದಾಯಕ ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕ ಉದ್ಯಮಗಳಿಗೆ ಮಹಾರತ್ನ, ನವರತ್ನ, ಮಿನಿರತ್ನ ಸ್ಥಾನ ನೀಡಲಾಯಿತು. ಇವುಗಳಿಗೆ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ ಕೈಗೊಳ್ಳುವಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಸ್ವಾಯತ್ತತೆ ದೊರೆಯಿತು.

caption.en: A PSU has 10 crore shares. Sell some to the public at ₹p each and see who owns what.

narration.en: Watch the government's stake shrink as shares are sold.

tryThis.en: Sell 2.5 crore at ₹80: the NCERT example.
Sell more than 5 crore shares. Is it still a public sector firm?
Why might selling too cheaply be criticised?

problem.en: The government owns 100% of a PSU with 10 crore shares. It sells 2.5 crore shares to the public at ₹80 each. What share does the government keep, and how much does it raise?

steps.en: Shares sold = 2.5 ÷ 10 = 25%, so the government keeps 75%.
Because the government keeps majority ownership, this is disinvestment, not full privatisation.

answer.en: Government keeps 75%; ₹200 crore raised through disinvestment.
